ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Mary McLeod Bethune Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for four months of wheeze, night cough and breathlessness on exertion in a 72-year-old woman with long-standing asthma that was never confirmed: examination, chest X-ray, ECG, blood tests and BNP, and planning of lung function testing and an echocardiogram. Concerns: Her breathing wakes her at night and stops her climbing stairs, and she has had to travel less; She has been told for years that it is asthma, or her weight, or her heart, and wants to know for certain which it is; She wants to keep going to Washington for the council's meetings. [S]

tr.td: Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: mild hyperinflation; heart size normal (cardiothoracic ratio 0.48); no pulmonary edema, effusion, mass or consolidation
Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 80 per minute; left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria; no Q waves, ST changes or arrhythmia
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with her consent

Spirometry before and 15 minutes after albuterol 400 mcg, with DLCO and FeNO, interpreted with GLI Global race-neutral equations: FEV1 1.30 L (64 percent predicted) rising to 1.57 L (+270 mL, +21 percent); FEV1/FVC 0.64 before and 0.72 after; DLCO 92 percent predicted; FeNO 46 ppb. Variable airflow obstruction without persistent obstruction: asthma, not COPD

Transthoracic echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 62 percent; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum 1.2 cm); grade 1 diastolic dysfunction; left atrium normal in size; right ventricle normal; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 28 mmHg; no significant valve disease
Written asthma action plan with peak flow zones (green above 270 L/min, yellow 170 to 270, red below 170, based on a provisional best of 340 to be confirmed), given and explained
Nasal endoscopy by the ear, nose and throat specialist: swollen mucosa and mucus in both middle meatuses; no polyps or mass; septum near midline
Inhaler technique assessment with her own inhaler: she did not shake it, breathed in fast and did not hold her breath; retrained with a spacer and checked by teach-back
Spirometry before bronchodilator after stabilization: FEV1 1.72 L (85 percent predicted); FEV1/FVC 0.73
COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, this season's formula
Respiratory syncytial virus vaccine, single dose

list.item: Wheeze, cough and breathlessness for four months: waking with cough and tight chest two or three nights a week, breathless on one flight of stairs, relieved by albuterol, worse with colds, dust and strong scents; known asthma for many years but never confirmed by lung function testing and never treated with an inhaled steroid. Asthma, COPD and heart failure to be distinguished: spirometry with bronchodilator response, FeNO and an echocardiogram booked: resolved, confirmed [S]
Blocked nose, thick postnasal drip and a reduced sense of smell for years, worse in the last year; no nosebleeds; never seen by an ear, nose and throat specialist: resolved, confirmed [S]

Gastro-esophageal reflux: heartburn and an acid taste two or three evenings a week, worse after late meals and lying down; no trouble swallowing, vomiting, black stools or weight loss: active, confirmed [S]
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 33.1); she wants to walk more and to keep up with her work, and agreed to talk about it: active, confirmed [S]

Moderate asthma exacerbation triggered by a cold: two days of worsening wheeze and night waking despite eight reliever inhalations a day, peak flow 205 L/min (60 percent of her best), oxygen saturation 94 percent; improved to 275 L/min in clinic; treated without admission; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

Asthma, confirmed: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1 64 percent predicted, rising 270 mL or 21 percent after bronchodilator, with a normal post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.72 and normal DLCO); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 46 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.42 x10^3/uL, total IgE 210, house dust mite sensitization); not COPD and not heart failure. Uncontrolled at diagnosis on albuterol alone: active, confirmed [S]

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: clinic blood pressure 152/88 and 146/86, home average 144/84; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with grade 1 diastolic dysfunction and a normal ejection fraction (62 percent); BNP 48 pg/mL: active, confirmed [S]
Hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 144 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent with hypertension: active, confirmed [S]

Chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps: years of congestion, postnasal drip and reduced smell, with mucosal swelling and mucus in both middle meatuses and no polyps on nasal endoscopy: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Retired college president who still chairs a national women's organization and travels to Washington, D.C., for its board meetings every month or two; lives in her own house on the campus in Daytona Beach and stays in the organization's Washington headquarters when she is there [S]

Lives alone; separated from her husband long before his death decades ago; a son and grandchildren live nearby; colleagues and church members visit daily. No relative is named or given a role in her care [S]

Grew up in a large farming family in South Carolina whose parents had been enslaved; has spent her life working against segregation, and has met clinicians who dismissed her breathlessness as her weight or her age [S]
Never smoked; no vaping; no wood stove at home; no alcohol; no occupational dust or chemical exposure [S]
Triggers she has noticed: colds, dust when papers and books are moved, strong perfume at meetings, and humid summer air; no pets; the house has central air conditioning [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for four months of wheeze, night cough and breathlessness on exertion in a 72-year-old woman with long-standing asthma that was never confirmed: examination, chest X-ray, ECG, blood tests and BNP, and planning of lung function testing and an echocardiogram

Diagnosis visit: spirometry, FeNO and echocardiogram results with the pulmonology consultation; asthma confirmed, heart failure excluded, hypertensive heart disease found; start of budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever
Six-week asthma review: control, inhaler technique and adherence, the ear, nose and throat result, blood pressure and reflux
Review six weeks after an exacerbation: control, repeat spirometry and FeNO, biologic assessment, blood pressure and the post-exacerbation plan
Same-day sick visit for an asthma exacerbation with a cold
Pulmonology consultation in two weeks with spirometry before and after bronchodilator, DLCO and FeNO, to confirm or refute asthma, separate it from COPD and heart disease, and plan treatment

Work-up of wheeze and breathlessness: chest X-ray, ECG, blood count with eosinophils, BNP, TSH and kidney function today; transthoracic echocardiogram before the consultation; albuterol continued as needed until testing, holding it for six hours before spirometry
Home blood pressure readings twice daily for a week, with a validated upper-arm cuff, because clinic readings are raised
Equity safeguards: spirometry read with race-neutral GLI Global equations, plain explanation of every result, and a check at each visit that her symptoms are not put down to her weight or age

GINA track 1: budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg as maintenance and reliever (one inhalation twice daily and one as needed, no more than 12 a day), albuterol stopped; inhaler technique, adherence and Asthma Control Test at every visit; a written asthma action plan with peak flow zones; review six weeks after any change and within a week of any exacerbation
Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: amlodipine 5 mg daily (a beta-blocker avoided because of asthma), a lower-salt diet, home readings, and kidney function and potassium at follow-up
Cardiovascular prevention: atorvastatin 20 mg daily for a 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent

Upper airway and reflux: fluticasone nasal spray and saline rinses, ear, nose and throat review with nasal endoscopy; omeprazole for eight weeks for heartburn with meal timing and head-of-bed elevation, then stop if settled
Weight and fitness, as she chooses: a dietitian visit, a walking plan she can follow on campus and in Washington, and a later discussion of medicines for weight if she wants one

Biologic assessment: not indicated while asthma is controlled on low-to-medium dose ICS-formoterol with good technique; repeat blood eosinophils and refer for biologic therapy if asthma becomes uncontrolled on step 4 to 5 treatment or there are two or more exacerbations needing oral corticosteroids in a year
A confirmed diagnosis within three weeks: spirometry with bronchodilator response, FeNO and an echocardiogram, with the pulmonology consultation
Asthma confirmed by a 21 percent, 270 mL bronchodilator response and FeNO 46 ppb; heart failure excluded; hypertensive heart disease found, two weeks after the first visit
Asthma Control Test 20 or more, no night waking, and travel to Washington without breathlessness
Asthma Control Test 22; no night waking; travelled to two board meetings
Correct inhaler technique with her own inhaler at every visit, and a written asthma action plan she can use
Technique corrected with a spacer at six weeks; action plan written at diagnosis and used during the exacerbation
Blood pressure below 130/80 at home and in clinic
Not achieved: one moderate exacerbation with a cold, treated with five days of prednisone without admission

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; breathless on one flight of stairs and has cut back her travel because of night cough and breathlessness [S]
